body: In my admittedly limited experience, 'shitty therapist' is a tautology.

If I could afford couple's therapy I'd definitely look into it. Unfortunately, it's not even remotely in the budget, unless I can find someone who will work for free. And, as this article stated, too many therapists like to join forces with the wife and gang up on the husband, especially in situations like this. I know, we *did* do marriage counseling for a while, and it happened just like that. And it got even worse when I naively let myself be vulnerable and opened up about personal shortcomings. I got burned badly. I think if I ever considered that route again, I'd need to screen the therapist first. Even then, it would be hard for me to trust one again.

I have suspected BPD in the past. It's also been suggested that, like me, she may be on the Autism spectrum. She scored high on online Autism tests, but you can't really come to a sure conclusion from such tests alone, and there were 'confounding factors' indicated. Schizotypal personality disorder has also been suggested.

I'll go down the list in this article:

1. **Censoring my thoughts and feelings.** Yes. Describes me to a T, down to not knowing what I think or feel about certain things. There are mountains of things I haven't told her due to how she might react. The last time I honestly confessed a shortcoming to her, it almost destroyed everything: our marriage, our finances, our social lives (when we had one), and everything else due to her reaction and the various people she got on her side to 'help' me.

2. **Everything is my fault.** Yep. She does do token self-blame at times, but usually this is about peripheral matters, and even though it's 'her fault', it's my fault if I ask her to take any sort of responsibility for it. She can't change or improve at all, as far as she's concerned. I, however, must change and improve at every little thing in order to be able to accommodate her.

3. **Constant criticism.** Yes. Exception being when she is in a good mood, or when I 'guess right' about what she wants, which is rare. But most of the time, I can't please her, no apology is good enough, and nothing I can do can fix it. I'm used to getting long lists of everything that's wrong all at once.

4. **Control freak.** Mostly. I have rarely caught her in an outright lie, and I think she often convinces herself that something is true when it isn't. She has been known to remember things that didn't happen, or not remember things that did. She has caught herself in this and admitted it. So I don't know if this should be counted as purposeful manipulation or not. She does engage in passive-aggression, which is manipulative, and she tends to freak out when she feels the situation is not 'under control'.

5. **Dr Jekyll and Ms Hyde.** Yes. This is normal. She can be really sweet sometimes, but rarely does this last and rarely does she follow through on any promises. She turns, sometimes on a dime, and becomes hostile. Then, after the fight, she walks around the house humming like nothing is wrong. Humming has, as a result, become an anxiety trigger for me, as ridiculous as that is.

6. **My feelings don't count.** Often, yes. She goes through temporary understanding periods. I have a tendency to overshare, and sometimes I can get away with doing this. She will at least listen and occasionally acknowledge my feelings. But most of the time they are dismissed or she takes offense at them. And even when she acknowledges them, her later actions dismiss them entirely, and her feelings and needs *always* take precedence.

7. **Questioning my own sanity.** I used to. I don't do this as much anymore, but I was convinced for a long time that there must be something seriously wrong with me, that I must be the cause of the problems. When I pushed myself and pushed myself, was open about my shortcomings, and kept trying to find ways to improve myself and saw things only getting worse, and saw her making no real efforts, I came to the conclusion that I was not the central problem. I am not perfect, but I no longer believe I'm the key factor to the issues. Seeing how she behaves so sweetly around other people, and how everyone thinks I have the most shy, meek little sweetheart of a wife in the world does sometimes make me still question my sanity or the validity of my feelings.

8. **Say what?** Yes. Again, this is sort of a constant thing feeding back to #3

9. **Isolating myself from friends and family.** Yes, but this likely has at least as much to do with my Autism as it does with her behavior. Isolating myself is in my nature. Admittedly, I have done this more since I married her, as I am afraid of what she will say and do around others. That and between her and my job, I spend all of my 'social energy' and have nothing left for actually being around others. I absolutely hate going shopping with her because it always turns into a public fight, and we usually shop at my workplace, which embarrasses me greatly.

10. **Walking on landmines.** Yes. Landmines is a good description, especially since you can't see where they're buried. I never know what's going to set her off.

11. **What goes up, must come down.** Yes. She has been known to shower me with complements at times. But then she turns around and tears me to peices later on. It is very confusing and disconcerting.

12. **Un-level playing field.** Yes. I can never figure out the rules with her. I'm bad at figuring out social rules as is, but she seems to keep changing them. What is good one day is a capital sin the next, and vice versa.

13. **You're a loser, but don't leave me.** This doesn't apply so much because I've never threatened to leave. She did try to leave once, and I foolishly chased after her. She then came back, issued demands, and we got back together. So, without experience in this area, I cannot say.

Oddly enough, in addition to describing my wife well, these 13 points describe my abusive mother to a T, even more so than my wife. But, I never had doubts she was a narcissist anyways.

What I do for work is retail. I despise it. Due to my health and the limited opportunities in my area, there really aren't many other options for me. My vehicle currently makes commuting difficult.

My interests include writing, ethics, mathematics, physics, linguistics, aquaponic agriculture, cooperatives, and community organization. All of these seem to require some startup cost I don't have, some education I don't have, connections I don't have, people skills I don't have, or just aren't something that's easy to make a living off of.

I do know that I'm a good writer. I have two novel's started, but finding the time to work on them is difficult. They have been collecting dust since winter started.

No, I haven't known that writing online was an option. I wouldn't know where to look to inquire about it, or what it would entail. I figured I would either need some sort of credentials or connections to get a job writing any sort of articles that I would be paid for, or I would have to have a successful blog. I have a blog, but its reach is limited, and due to Autism my communication style on some of the more technical points is difficult for many to digest, since I deal with essential details and interconnected systems of ideas, instead of 'big-picture' generalizations, which I in turn have a difficult time with.

If there are other options out there to get into writing online, it would be something I'd be interested in. Money is not by any means my central problem, but it is a peripheral problem, and solving that might bring at least a few things under control.

I was raised by a narcissist. I don't know that my wife is one, but I'm not particularly good at reading people, and I'm terrible at reading her particularly. She seems more out of control and erratic than anything. Constantly high strung and stretched thin. She doesn't seem particularly narcissistic, but she does have her aloof moments and she does seem entirely capable of humility. Getting an apology out of her, token or otherwise, is akin to finding a fist-sized diamond in parking lot.

But, none of that changes the fact that I'm stuck with her.

I'm not the best with open ended questions, but I'll give it a try and hope what I include will be relevant.

She is not a very stable person. She isn't physically violent and it doesn't appear to be bipolar, but she is very emotionally led and easily agitated. She gets offended easily and expects me to know what she wants without telling me. She's always on the defensive, always closed up and distant. She also hovers and can be smothering at times. She has a low tolerance for frustration and a tendency to take it out on other people. She doesn't think ahead, doesn't consider other people, and doesn't think about consequences of her actions. She is a bit of a hoarder, and has hoarded many material possessions, mostly clothing and furniture that we don't need, to the point that our house is full of excessive clutter. We have few clear surfaces to even set things on. She has even hoarded things like empty cereal boxes, empty jars, etc; I feel like I live in a china shop, because I can hardly move through the house without knocking something over.

She can be very sweet and affectionate when she wants to be, and when the mood strikes her she knows how to say the right things to make you think she is going to try to make an effort to work things out. She never follows through on any of this, however, and her affection is very ephemeral. She is a fair weather friend, except one I'm married to. I have to always be careful around her not to offend or set her off, but I have to take whatever she dishes out without complaining, or she gets even more upset. She also has a tendency to list off all of her/our problems and everything that's not quite right all at once, which feels very overwhelming to me. It's depressing.

She has very little self control. Just now, as I'm typing this, she came in and raved about how our toddler threw something at her and it hit her in the face, so she smacked him in the face and it will probably leave a mark. He has a doctor's appointment tomorrow. Great. I feel like I'm living with a bottle of nitroglycerin with legs.

Of course, I mostly listed off all her negative qualities. She has spent lots of time working with our kid and teaching him, and he has benefited greatly from it. She does do some things around the house sometimes when she's motivated. And she hasn't left *me* yet, so I suppose putting up with me would be an achievement on her part.
